original_question: Let G be a finitely generated group with Schreier growth gap f, meaning that for every faithful action of G on a set X, the function Vol_{G,X}(n) is bounded below by f(n) up to the paper's asymptotic comparison, and call the gap nontrivial when f is superlinear. Are there hyperbolic groups that have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap but do not have an exponential Schreier growth gap?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Question 6.3: "Are there hyperbolic groups which satisfy a nontrivial Schreier growth gap, but not an exponential one?"
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the correct target: Section 6, Question 6.3. It correctly focuses on hyperbolic groups, on the distinction between a nontrivial Schreier growth gap and an exponential Schreier growth gap, and it correctly uses the paper’s viewpoint that the gap is defined through lower bounds for the growth functions of all faithful actions on sets. It also correctly interprets "nontrivial" as superlinear, matching Definition 6.1.
missing_details: The paper first fixes a finite generating set S of G and defines the action-growth function explicitly by vol_{G,X}(n)=max_{x in X}|B_S(n)·x|, where B_S(n) is the radius-n ball in G; your draft refers to vol_{G,X}(n) but does not define it.
To be fully stand-alone, the asymptotic comparison must be stated explicitly: one writes f ≼ g if there exists C>0 such that f(n) ≤ C g(Cn) for all n≥1, and vol_{G,X} ≽ f means f ≼ vol_{G,X}.
The paper’s setup allows arbitrary faithful G-sets X; transitivity is not assumed, so the associated Schreier graph may be disconnected.
The phrase "exponential Schreier growth gap" should be spelled out as meaning a Schreier growth gap comparable to an exponential function in the same coarse sense.

Your draft introduces an abstract gap function f first and then asks the hyperbolic-group existence question. That is mathematically fine, but it is slightly broader than the paper’s official wording, which asks the existence question directly.

If you want the question to track the paper’s local intent more tightly, it helps to keep the nearby motivation in view: the paragraph after Definition 6.1 notes that Property (T), and more generally Property FM, give exponential Schreier growth gaps, while cyclically distorted elements give nontrivial gaps. Question 6.3 asks whether hyperbolic groups can exhibit a strictly intermediate phenomenon.
refined_question: Let G be a finitely generated hyperbolic group, fix a finite generating set S, and for every faithful action G on a set X define vol_{G,X}(n)=max_{x in X}|B_S(n)·x|, where B_S(n) is the ball of radius n in G. Write f ≼ g if there exists C>0 such that f(n) ≤ C g(Cn) for all n≥1, and say that G has Schreier growth gap f if vol_{G,X} ≽ f for every faithful G-set X. Call the gap nontrivial if f is superlinear. Does there exist a hyperbolic group G that has a nontrivial Schreier growth gap but does not have an exponential Schreier growth gap?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Question 6.3 in Section 6. The surrounding discussion first defines the action-growth function vol_{G,X}(n), then Definition 6.1 introduces the notion of a Schreier growth gap and says that the gap is nontrivial when the lower-bound function is superlinear. The paragraph immediately after Definition 6.1 explains that Property (T), and even the weaker Property FM, give exponential Schreier growth gaps, while cyclically distorted elements give nontrivial ones; the neighboring Question 6.2 asks for hyperbolic examples without infinite subgroups with Property FM. Your draft does not target that neighboring FM question; it targets the next and narrower existence question, namely whether hyperbolic groups can have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap without having an exponential one. No explicit equivalent reformulation is proved in this paper, so the refined version should remain a sharpened restatement of Question 6.3 rather than a new variant.
